source.cleaned_file: goldbound/028 - I Tried Farming A WoW Token In Blasted Lands - Here's What Happened - Goldbound 27.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So, running the numbers, the odds of not getting the chest to drop after 29 runs is .165%. Yeah, we're a little bit unlucky on the Nightslayer chest. Of course, our previous runs aren't going to change the drop rate of future runs, but looking at the sample size of 29 kills with no drop is pretty wild. But we'll try again next week. But there is one thing we don't need luck for, a pretty popular Blasted Lands gold farm and one that some gold goblins might not want advertised, but as Goldy says, the auction house and gold farms, they're PvP. So, let's go. It's war bear leather farming time. And for this one, we're straight back down into the tainted forest. There's quite a few mobs down here, which are also honoring the namesake as tainted. The one in particular that we want is the tainted black bear. This guy, when skinned, has a 21% chance to drop war bear leather. And much like living essence, war bear leather is used in a few rare classic transmog recipes, giving it some pretty respectable gold values. And while the prices on war bear leather are usually pretty variable, largely depending on how many people are actively farming and listing them, at the moment, it has a very solid market value of about 65 to 75 gold each. And in the area that we're farming the bears, there's actually a few other tainted mobs that we want to tag, a few of which can add some value to the farm, one of which being the tainted nightstalker. Now, these spiders have an 8% chance to drop iron web spider silk, yet another classic transmog crafting material. The current market value of spider silk is about 50 gold. So, a couple extra of these per hour could definitely go a long way. The general idea here is to roam around the central forest area, tagging and skinning as many of the tainted black bears as possible, which, aside from war bear leather, they also skin into rugged leather sometimes. And with the boar target macro updated to just target tainted, we actually take down the spiders whenever they're near anyways.

source.quote: And the only downside for Goldie is that this area is actually pretty large, and the distance between bears is pretty big. So, our rates are definitely going to be slower than something like a druid, who can instant cast flight form between the black bears to get higher rates. Plus, for this farm in particular, we do want to have high levels of skinning to avoid getting just scraps. I'm running 300 here just to be safe, since it's not too hard to power level from 1 to 300 in Sunken Temple. All right, with the war bear leather farm, how much gold per hour can I pull in on Goldie? Well, we managed to get 35 war bear leather for the hour, which results in about 2400 gold just from the leather. We also got 13 iron web spider silks, about 780 gold, and 253 rugged leather, about 1500 gold, and a few random living essences as well from the tree ants. On top of that, we have some decent vendor trash, bringing the total gold per hour to 4,970 gold per hour. Definitely not a bad farm, and I imagine it could be optimized quite a bit with a druid who's faster, but the clams and mining is still outpacing it. Also, the war bear leather itself is a bit of a slower mover, so even if the gold per hour was higher, you would have to take the angle of stocking up on the leather to hopefully sell it over time, but still, a good farm to add to the variety here in Blasted Lands. And while we have skinning here in Blasted Lands, there are a couple of other skinnable mobs in the zone. There's boars and basilisks, but neither of them have a spot that looks to lend itself to a nice hyper spawn, and they don't have any rare skin like war bear leather to sweeten the pot. So, for now, I'll leave them be.

source.quote: Even if we go dry on the wealth doing this kind of a farm, we still get some decent consistent gold this way. And since we got two copies of the Time-Locked Box on my transmog alt, I'm going to list one as the box and one as the wealth after running and caging it, just so we can actually try to sell both at the same time. But, this kind of multi-farm optimization doesn't end here. Because, like I said, I'm farming a thousand clams to open and test the rates. So, while I'm down farming clams, every 5 to 10 minutes, I can pop out, clear the Arcane Crystals from the Tainted Forest, and have a look for some of the rares. And after all this testing, the rares seem to be on a respawn timer of about 1 to 5 hours per rare. So, it really is just a matter of doing a couple laps every hour to hopefully time the respawn on a couple of them. And it seems we can average about one to three rare settings per hour pretty consistently using these methods. So, I'm going to go ahead, lock in, and min-max some of these farms making use of the Tainted Forest for rich Thorium Ore as much as I can. I want to get as many Arcane Crystals as my bag can hold. But, speaking of Thorium and this multi-farm version of Blasted Lands, I actually noticed something very interesting. So, it seems that no matter which version of the Dormi time we're in, the Tainted Forest is always the same one. It's the classic version. It has the rares and has the Arcane Crystals.

source.quote: All right. So, I ended up farming for a few hours and pulled in 2,000 thorium ore. Alongside that, we also got 70 arcane crystals and a couple of drain of this spheres. And the results for swapping back and forth between the two timelines compared to mining in regular Blasted Lands only, when swapping back and forth, we got about 410 thorium ore per hour, giving about 50 extra thorium ore per hour and moving the gold per hour closer to 8,000 gold. So, this is definitely a good route to add in and juice it from time to time. Speaking of farming up a fair amount here in the Blasted Lands, we have a few items to open up. First and foremost is the 1,000 clams. Now, this is actually mostly for my own curiosity and to get an estimated drop chance so that in the future we can look at the price of clams, the price of pearls, and make an educated decision on whether to open them or not. So, let's get cracking these 1,000 clams open. And with current value, these clams are worth about 15,000 gold at 15 gold a piece, but region market value historically has been closer to 20 gold each per clam, which would make it about 20,000 gold worth of clams. But for today, with an average list price on golden pearls being 500 gold, that means we need to pull in 30 or more golden pearls from these 1,000 clams to break even. And the results?

source.quote: And the blue ones, since they sell for 700 gold each, I'm honestly just going to sell them as is. The sale rate on them is high enough that they're basically liquid gold. Even if you got lucky opening them with some decent value transmog, well, we might have to wait several months to actually sell it. So, especially in Goldie's case, gold today, and maybe more specifically, gold in this week's mailbox clear, will be more valuable than gold in two to three months. With that being said, for the green BOEs, I did open up 85 of them from about 30 hours of farming in the zone so far, and got 8,300 gold in average sale value. So, assuming we sell most of this transmog for region sale averages over time, which is pretty reasonable, as most of this should actually sell closer to market value, that gives us a baseline of value at just under 100 gold per shard, which is quite a bit higher than their nine gold sale price. So, this seems to be a profitable shuffle for Goldie, although it will spread the gold out over time, kind of like we talked about. Speaking of profits though, I do think it's about that time that we take a look at the mailbox and see how much gold we're sitting on. We have some pretty solid farms here in Blasted Lands, so I for one am hoping for a good chunk of change. I have about 15,000 gold in the bags right now, and the wild token is hovering between 250 and 260,000 gold right now. It's back up 20 to 30k from midnight lows. And we've been doing a lot of farming, so we have several pages of trade goods pending. So, let's work through these one page at a time and 100 openings at a time. We can already see a very good chunk of change from the arcane crystals. And let me tell you, you will see a lot of arcane crystals and thorium ore this mailbox clear. And even quite a few of the flawless granite spheres being sold. And who knows what the buyers of these ended up pulling from the spheres, but we have over 7,000 gold in legit currency right now to show for them, so I'm not too mad about selling them. So, let's get these first 100 looted and see where we're at.
